answer: Each agent must lock an equal bond before accepting paid work, whether it analyzes glacier images, maps a river delta, or dates a relic. A contract freezes that bond through a dispute window and slashes it when a submitted result fails a predefined, verifiable check. Creating identities is cheap, but activating a thousand requires a thousand bonds; coordinated fraud risks losing that collateral, while locked funds impose an opportunity cost even if no attack succeeds.
